title.narrative: Strengthening conservation and resilience of forest landscapes in the sub-humid mountainous zone of Togo

description.narrative: 1. Local communities are at the core of the approach selected under the project. Greater involvement of local communities in decision-making processes and in the management of forest resources will have the double benefit of promoting conservation and supporting the development of sustainable sources of income that improve communities’ livelihoods. The development of diversified, biodiversity-friendly and resilient production systems will generate sustainable sources of income, particularly for women and youth who are priority targets of the project, and will allow community needs in wood and NTFPs to be met, thereby reducing the pressure on remaining forest patches. As a result, the project will also contribute to food and nutrition security. Furthermore, given the significant contribution of coffee and cacao to agricultural exportation, improved management of agroforests will enhance benefits to the national economy and the local population. 2. The project interventions will enable local communities to become actors of the decision-making processes for the management of their environment. Communities’ involvement in decision-making processes for the management of gazetted forests and the establishment/strengthening of community-managed forests will increase their sense of ownership and responsibility in the becoming of their natural resources. In addition, it will reduce conflicts around land tenure between the government and local communities. Through these participatory decision-making processes, the project will also contribute to identifying a combination of actions and land-use practices that best support sustainable and equitable access to, and utilization of, socio-economic benefits derived from forest landscapes while conservating natural resources and maintaining ecosystem functioning. 3. The community groups involved in the microprojects – particularly women and youth – will also be empowered through institutional and technical capacity building to improve their sources of income in a manner that they will have chosen and worked towards. The project will establish all the required policy documents, decision-making, management, technical and financial support, and monitoring systems to maintain the participatory approach for decision-making and the improved livelihood practices beyond the end of the project. 4. The agroecological practices to be adopted under the project will support healthier soil and water bodies, thereby benefitting human health. In addition, the project objective to conserve ecosystem functioning and the biodiversity of remaining Guinean forest landscapes will support the provision of ecosystems good and services (e.g. food production, biodiversity conservation, protection of water catchments, soil and water conservation) to sustain a healthy environment. By protecting and supporting the restoration of natural forests, the project will act towards maintaining communities’ opportunities to experience natural beauty, fresh air and biodiversity. 5. With regards to climate change, the promoted production practices will increase the resilience of these systems to climate change effects (e.g. intense rains, longer drought periods) through species diversification, agroecology practices and more efficient use of water and soil resources. The project will also support increased ecological resilience by improving the management systems of remaining forest patches, supporting the restoration of degraded areas and enhancing the connectivity between remnant forests along the corridor from the South of Zone IV to FMNP as well as with native forests on the other side of the border, in Ghana. Implementation of integrated management systems for native forests (241,945 ha) and agroforests (55,000 ha) in Guinean forest landscapes with strong involvement of local communities to preserve biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, carbon storage, and promote sustainable and resilient sources of income for forest-dependent men and women.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
